Olivia (support): Customer GlyphInc on dedicated pool dp-eu-3 is seeing 429s and long queue times since ~2026-03-15T09:12Z. They say traffic is within their expected usage and plan shows high units. Can SRE triage? :eyes:
Raj (sre): Can you paste tenant_id + example request_ids?
Olivia (support): tenant_id: glyph-42. request_id examples: r1=da3f, r2=bf10. I pulled tail of router logs, see a bunch of `rate_limit_exceeded` events with per-tenant key.
Olivia (support): quick excerpt:
```json
{"time":"2026-03-15T09:12:34Z","tenant":"glyph-42","code":429,"reason":"PER_TENANT_RATE_EXCEEDED","pool":"dp-eu-3"}
```
Mei (eng-infra): Noted. Any recent plan/quotas changes for GlyphInc? Could be denom mismatch (minutes vs hours).
Carlos (cs): They migrated billing plan yesterday at 02:00 UTC. Billing UI shows `Custom-Enterprise` with 1,000 units/hour. Ops ticket said migration completed.
Raj (sre): I'll check mapping service for tenant->rateprofile. Sometimes the rateprofile tag is stale after a migration. Running quick query on rate-mapper.
deploy-bot: deployment raterouter-v2 rolled to dp-eu-3 at 2026-03-15T08:55Z
Raj (sre): Found it: glyph-42 still bound to legacy profile `rp:legacy_minute_100` (100/min) instead of `rp:enterprise_1000_hour`. Looks like migration script skipped tag update.
Mei (eng-infra): That would explain. The per-tenant limiter uses the profile denom when computing tokens. If profile is minute-based, bursts will be capped heavily.
Olivia (support): Customer reports the 429s drop off ~09:18UTC when they reduced concurrency, consistent.
Raj (sre): I'll patch the mapping to point glyph-42 -> rp:enterprise_1000_hour and trigger a refresh to the ratecache. ETA 10m.
Mei (eng-infra): Also setting a short warmup so autoscaler doesn't evict warm workers. Suggest follow-up: add a migration step to invalidate ratecache for migrated tenants.
Raj (sre): Patch applied, ratecache refresh kicked, seeing decrease in 429s for the sample request_ids.
Olivia (support): Confirmed with customer: errors dropped to near zero and latency back to normal. Customer is relieved. :thumbsup:
Carlos (cs): I'll log a post-mortem with the billing team and propose audit for future migrations.
Mei (eng-infra): Posting repro and fix snippet here for runbook:
```bash
# fix mapping
curl -X POST https://internal-api/rate-mapper/update -d '{"tenant":"glyph-42","rate_profile":"rp:enterprise_1000_hour"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP'
# refresh ratecache
curl -X POST https://internal-api/ratecache/refresh -d '{"tenant":"glyph-42"}'
```
Raj (sre): Root cause: migration tool failed to update tenant tag (tag race + missing cache invalidation). Impact: dedicated pool dp-eu-3 experienced per-tenant throttling for glyph-42.
Olivia (support): Marking as resolved for now, will follow up on runbook changes. Adding customer-facing summary and next steps.
Carlos (cs): Customer asks for a credit for the ~6 minute degradation window; I'll escalate to billing.
Olivia (support): Thanks team. Adding labels: incident:dedicated-rate-mismatch, owner:eng-infra, severity:low-medium.
